mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over the prior 3 months reduces the discount rate applied to future corporate cash flows, lowering the present value of expected earnings and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by at least 0.25% over the past 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during a similar 3-month pre-increase period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10,000 jobs while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points within the same month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns under such labor conditions are not significantly higher than during comparable non-strengthening periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1,200K for three consecutive months suggests expanding credit availability and consumer confidence, which accelerates corporate investment and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive in more than 70% of similar monthly expansion episodes (rolling 12-months).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in two consecutive months signals supply-side weakness that reduces corporate earnings visibility, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during such contractions are not statistically lower than during prior supply expansions (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 0.3% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to exhibit negative forward returns over the next 20 days due to market anticipation of rate hikes that erode equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by > 0.3% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite the inflation signal (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 3.5% followed by a sustained rise in labor force participation (PAYEMS) suggests a demographic or confidence-driven expansion in the working-age population, which supports equity market optimism and positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.5% and PAYEMS increases by > 5,000 in the following month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during comparable labor expansion episodes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a sustained monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising while UNRATE remains above 5%), S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days tend to be negative due to reduced credit availability and rising risk aversion.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases for 4 consecutive months and UNRATE > 5% throughout
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not consistently negative across 5 such regimes (rolling average p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (monthly) for four months indicates structural supply constraints, which lowers earnings expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during such episodes are not statistically lower than during prior supply expansion phases (p > 0.05).
